findings: The summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:17 should distinguish written permission and terms from a Stripe Mandate payload and from explicit customer authorization of the local merchant-of-record provider. The May Checkout branch calls for an upfront opt-in and a retained written agreement. Off-session terms include scope, anticipated frequency/timing and amount determination, plus cancellation policy for subscriptions. Checkout requires authorizing the local provider for future payments (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:29-46,60-94). The Nigeria overview (raw/stripe-payments-countries-nigeria-2026-11-07.md:5-15,76-83,105-117) separately supplies partner identity, invite-request scope and the Naira card matrix, without proving account eligibility or a payment. Partner-MoR differs from Stripe Managed Payments (wiki/sources/source-stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:14-23; wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:8-14,40-42).

May Checkout creates a setup-mode Session for the Stripe Customer, which the merchant maps to its user. Test success is the SetupIntent transition from requires_action to succeeded (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:42-94). Direct API setup creates an ng_card SetupIntent with Customer and usage, passes the SetupIntent secret to browser Stripe.js, and shows confirmNgCardSetup with return_url and online infer_from_client (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:110-151,220-270). Separate charge-and-save starts/attempts a PaymentIntent with Customer, confirm and setup_future_usage=off_session, a return URL and optional mandate_data. Its sample includes explicit IP/user agent, NGN and automatic capture (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:332-370). These are distinct setup, payment and consent identities. The current summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:24,28-35 should scope the successful SetupIntent transition to the successful test/setup outcome and keep redirects distinct from that outcome.

The baseline wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:35 and wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:58-59 overstate a code sample as a mandate_data requirement. The May PaymentIntent prose explicitly says optional mandate_data (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:339-367), and the distinct November Create PaymentIntent reference says the object is optional and usable with confirm=true (raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-create-2026-11-07.md:627-650). The May browser SetupIntent sample infers acceptance metadata from the client (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:248-265). A separately captured November Billing SetupIntents variant performs server confirmation with explicit IP and user agent in its example and then uses Stripe.js for the redirect/mandate authorization (raw/stripe-billing-subscriptions-ng-card-variant-c8486b9656-2026-11-07.md:36-58). Date and qualify by route/client-server role, retaining consumer's written permission regardless of optional request payload. The typed field, recorded permission and authorized mandate are separate.

In the manual redirect branch, require both PaymentIntent.status=requires_action and next_action.type=redirect_to_url, then take the redirect URL from that next_action. Browser return can include the PaymentIntent ID and client secret. Use server webhook status to verify payment outcome (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:272-330). The mapped source and reciprocal concept omit the status check and verification boundary (wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:37-39; wiki/concepts/stripe-nigeria-payment-methods.md:63-65). The later charge makes and confirms a new PaymentIntent using the saved PaymentMethod ID from the preceding Intent and its Customer, with off_session=true when the customer is absent. Server detach deactivates the reusable payment method and sends mandate.updated and payment_method.detached (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:372-396). The current summary wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:41-47 should distinguish conditional off_session and detach from payment outcomes or subscription cancellation.

The mapped source reproduces historical writable payment_method_types across Checkout setup, SetupIntent creation, charge-and-save and saved reuse (wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:23-43). Preserve the May examples in context, including standalone manual redirect, with a reciprocal API-version warning. The May requests send the field on Checkout Session Create (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:79-90), SetupIntent Create (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:133-147), and PaymentIntent Create (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:272-295,339-368,372-392). The separate November-captured Checkout changelog documents HTTP 400 on Checkout Session Create at its linked 2026-09-30.endive endpoint and retains payment_method_types in the response (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions-2026-11-07.md:5-23). The Intent changelog's 2026-09-30.endive Create links and REST table document HTTP 400 with payment_method_types_no_longer_supported for the state-changing request, while the PaymentIntent/SetupIntent property remains read-only. Preserve that changelog's separate Impact reference to 2026-08-26.preview as a version ambiguity (raw/stripe-changelog-endive-2026-09-30-removes-the-payment-method-types-parameter-from-payment-intents-and-setup-intents-2026-11-07.md:5-36). The raw pair supplies neither a November applicable API version nor a migrated ng_card flow.

Section wiki/sources/source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md:37-39 places the optional manual redirect under Save Paths. The May example is a standalone PaymentIntent payment that creates and immediately uses a PaymentMethod. Its request omits Customer, setup_future_usage and mandate_data from the separately described charge-and-save route. The example neither confirms a SetupIntent nor demonstrates future-use attachment or saving (raw/stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments-2025.md:272-330,332-370). Preserve both requires_action and redirect_to_url gates and server webhook verification; the browser return is a navigation signal. Carry the same scope into the reciprocal Nigeria concept's manual redirect description.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/ng-card/set-up-future-payments says to save Naira cards for later charges and links Checkout and Direct API (new raw lines 5-14). May shows written customer permission with off-session terms, the app's mapping to a Stripe Customer and explicit authorization of the local merchant-of-record provider for future payments on the Checkout route. Its setup-mode Session invokes customer authentication and the successful test reaches SetupIntent succeeded from requires_action (old raw lines 29-94). Direct API saves without an initial charge using a server-created Customer-linked SetupIntent and browser confirmNgCardSetup with its client secret and mandate data. A separate PaymentIntent can attempt a charge while saving with setup_future_usage (old raw lines 110-151, 220-270 and 332-370). The merchant can later create a separate PaymentIntent using the saved PaymentMethod ID and Customer, setting off_session when the customer is absent, or detach the reusable method server-side, which generates two events (old raw lines 372-396). The existing source-stripe-ng-card-set-up-future-payments.md captures the route types but needs the partner permission, optional API payload, redirect verification and conditional off-session qualifications. Setup success does not establish a later payment.
